Synopsis:
    The Trump administration has filed an emergency application with the U.S. Supreme Court seeking to reinstate USPS mail-in ballot restrictions ahead of November 2026 midterm elections. A federal judge (Talwani) has twice blocked the rule, which stems from a March executive order. The rule would require states to share voter lists with USPS and mandate barcoded ballot envelopes, with non-compliant ballots subject to non-delivery. Justice Jackson set a Wednesday response deadline. The Supreme Court is now the decisive arbiter. North Carolina has already begun mailing ballots, adding urgency.
